title: Saint Cajetan, Priest
short_summary: Saint Cajetan was a sixteenth-century Italian priest who co-founded the Theatines to reform clerical life and worked to help the poor avoid predatory debt.
key_facts: The Church permits his optional memorial on August 7.
He was born in Vicenza, Italy, in 1480, and trained first as a lawyer.
In 1524 he co-founded the Theatines, a community of priests devoted to reforming clerical life.
He worked to establish charitable lending institutions to help the poor avoid predatory debt.

sections.heading: From law to reform of the clergy
sections.body: Cajetan trained as a lawyer before turning to the priesthood and to the reform of clerical life, in a period when many in the Church recognized the need for renewal.

sections.heading: Founder of the Theatines
sections.body: In 1524 Cajetan co-founded the Congregation of Clerics Regular, known as the Theatines, a community of priests committed to apostolic poverty and disciplined pastoral life. His companion in this work, Gian Pietro Carafa, later became Pope Paul IV.

sections.heading: Charity toward the poor
sections.body: Cajetan supported charitable lending arrangements meant to offer the poor an alternative to predatory moneylenders, joining spiritual reform with practical concern for those in economic need.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Reform beginning with the clergy
catholic_connection_sections.body: Cajetan's work points to a theme repeated across Church history: renewal of the whole Church often begins with the reform of priestly life.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Charity and justice together
catholic_connection_sections.body: His concern for fair lending shows that Catholic charity includes structural concern for justice, not only individual almsgiving.
